Attach an annual NIS companion to Core discharges

Source: R/open-companion.R
nis_join_companion.Rd

Add selected companion fields to a lazy Core query.

Usage

nis_join_companion(.data, path, component, columns)

Arguments

.data

A lazy Core query from nis_open(), including its linkage fields.

path

Directory containing Parquet for one companion component, using the annual or Hive layout accepted by nis_open(). Keep Core and each companion in separate directories, with parts from the same release.

component

One of "hospital", "severity", or "dx_pr_grps".

columns

<tidy-select> Select one or more companion fields by name across the selected years. Linkage keys are included automatically and are outside the selection. Use the field's source spelling for bare names or all_of(). Selected fields keep their source names and must have names distinct from fields in .data.

Value

A lazy DuckDB-backed Core query with the requested columns added.

Details

Join Hospital data on YEAR and HOSP_NIS. Join Severity or Diagnosis and Procedure Groups data on YEAR and KEY_NIS. Use the same release for each annual Core and companion part. Unmatched discharges remain in the result with missing companion values. Hospital TOTAL_DISC counts sampled discharges and is excluded. The joined records still represent discharges.

See also

Prepare annual NIS files, Opening NIS data, HCUP NIS File Specifications.

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpepKHEX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpepKHEX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
hospitals <- nis |>
  dplyr::distinct(HOSP_NIS, beds = HOSP_BEDSIZE) |>
  dplyr::collect()

path <- tempfile()
dir.create(path)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpepKHEX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "hospitals", hospitals)
file <- DBI::dbQuoteString(con, file.path(path, "NIS_2020.parquet"))
DBI::dbExecute(con, paste("COPY hospitals TO", file, "(FORMAT PARQUET)"))
#> [1] 12
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

nis |>
  nis_join_companion(path, "hospital", beds) |>
  dplyr::count(beds) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>    beds     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     1    32
#> 2     2    32
#> 3     3    32
